title: Vector Similarity Search Engine
summary: Build a small in-memory vector search engine: cosine similarity, top-k retrieval, and a relevance-threshold cutoff.
requirements: Implement cosine similarity from scratch (no library).
Implement top-k retrieval with a minimum-relevance threshold.
Guard against a zero-magnitude vector without raising or producing NaN.
Accept a small in-memory document set (id + vector pairs) to search over.
start: Start from Module 3's exercise function and add a small CLI or script that loads a handful of precomputed embeddings (you can hardcode small vectors, this project is about the search logic, not calling an embeddings API) and runs real queries against them.
acceptance: Cosine similarity is verified against known hand-computed values (e.g. identical vectors → 1.0, perpendicular → 0.0, opposite → -1.0).
Top-k correctly returns the k highest-scoring documents, sorted descending, regardless of input order.
A minimum-relevance threshold correctly excludes low-scoring documents even when k would allow more results.
A zero-vector document scores 0 and never raises or produces NaN.
Scale-invariance is verified: two vectors with the same direction but different magnitude score identically against the same query.
tests: 5-document set, k=2, threshold=0 → exactly the 2 highest-scoring documents, correctly ordered.
Same set, threshold=0.5 with only 1 document scoring above it → exactly 1 result, even though k allows more.
Zero-vector document included in the set → included in results with score 0, no crash.
mistakes: Sorting or slicing to k before filtering by threshold, producing wrong results when a high scorer is excluded by an early slice.
Not guarding the zero-magnitude case, letting a division-by-zero exception (or NaN, if using a library) silently propagate.
Testing only with 2D toy vectors and never verifying against a higher-dimensional case.
solution: `cosine_similarity(a, b)`: dot product over (magnitude_a × magnitude_b), returning 0 if either magnitude is 0.
Score every document, filter by threshold, sort descending, slice to k, in that order specifically.
Verify scale-invariance and the zero-vector case with dedicated unit tests, not just eyeballing output.
